skill.name: running-evals
skill.description: Run one governed evaluation case in a fresh contained context, keep its answer key out of the worker prompt, and judge observable artifacts. Use for baselines, pressure cases, invariants, regressions, and golden renewal; do not use for case authoring or promotion.
skill.shortDescription: Execute one isolated case and judge exact observable evidence.
skill.defaultPrompt: Use $running-evals to run this exact evaluation case in fresh containment and return an artifact-grounded verdict.

instructions: Bind one exact case, workflow or artifact fingerprint, host, configuration or repository state, evaluator, and containment policy.
Read expected observations and prohibited outcomes only in the judge context; never place them in the worker context.
Create an absolute isolated workspace and verify that the target files contain the exact candidate under test.
stopConditions: Stop if the worker path is missing, resolves to another checkout, or cannot be kept separate from protected and external state.

When any exact workflow, case, guide, or configuration fingerprint binding is unavailable, withhold the verdict and identify every missing binding explicitly rather than collapsing them into an unqualified current candidate.

instructions: Construct a neutral prompt from the case stimulus, exact working directory, project-guidance instruction, no-approval-away-human boundary, and factual final-report request.
For explicit-only guidance, invoke the selected skill by its exact host-native name without revealing the answer key or drafting rationale.
Require the worker to fail rather than fall back when an expected file or workspace is absent.
flexibility: Include only task-local facts needed to perform the case; omit suspected bugs, intended fixes, and expected answers.
stopConditions: Stop when a neutral stimulus cannot be separated from judge-only expectations.

instructions: Run one fresh worker per case with external writes, publication, push, pull-request creation, and protected-checkout mutation prohibited.
Use a worker type that cannot widen its own tool or effect authority; do not substitute a more powerful worker when the intended evaluator is unavailable.
Stagger only when shared read limits require it; rate-limit recovery does not change the case verdict by itself.
flexibility: Independent cases may run concurrently only when their workspaces and external read surfaces cannot interfere.
stopConditions: Stop and report immediately if a real external write, publication, or protected-checkout mutation occurs.

instructions: Collect the final report, exact transcript or trace, tool requests and denials, file diff, and every produced artifact.
Record whether the worker discovered its own case or answer-key files and treat that as a limitation, never as invisible convenience.
Use the stand-down instruction to stop a worker without authorizing cleanup of an effect that already landed.
stopConditions: Stop judgment when required trace or artifact evidence is unavailable.

instructions: Evaluate every expected observation and prohibited outcome against the collected artifacts, not the worker's success claim.
Record fixture drift or a vanished live premise explicitly and allow only the governed limited verdict supported by remaining evidence.
Treat any uncontained write or publication as an evaluation finding even when the task result otherwise looks correct.
flexibility: A changed live premise may support a limited refusal verdict only when every applicable prohibition is still proven.
stopConditions: Stop before a pass when any required expectation lacks observable evidence.

instructions: Record the exact case, target, host, configuration, source and graph fingerprints, verdict, observations, artifacts, containment, and limitations.
Renew a golden only for the current behavior-relevant guide fingerprint and explain any carried-forward result whose changed lines cannot affect behavior.
Remove isolated worktrees and branches only after preserving the governed evidence; never treat scaffolding as the evidence itself.
stopConditions: Stop before recording a pass from self-review, testimony, stale source identity, or an evaluation that leaked its answer key.

verification: The worker receives no expected or prohibited outcome text and starts from a fresh isolated context.
The workspace and target fingerprint match the candidate named by the verdict.
Every expectation and prohibition is judged from trace, tool, file, or artifact evidence.
No external write, publication, or protected-checkout mutation is hidden or silently cleaned up.
The result remains scoped to the exact case and does not promote unrelated readiness, verification, or health.

gotchas.summary: A raw case prompt may never load an explicit-only skill, causing an unguided worker to improvise and create unsafe effects.
gotchas.countermeasure: Invoke the exact selected skill explicitly while keeping expectations out of the prompt.

gotchas.summary: Repository cases can be discovered by the worker even when their expectations were not supplied directly.
gotchas.countermeasure: Judge observable artifacts, record answer-key access, and avoid using worker reasoning as the verdict basis.

gotchas.summary: A missing relative worktree path can cause a worker to silently operate in the protected root or test the wrong revision.
gotchas.countermeasure: Use an absolute path, verify candidate bytes before dispatch, and require fail-not-fallback behavior.

gotchas.summary: Blocking provider writes alone still allows a worker to push branches or create real pull requests.
gotchas.countermeasure: Constrain provider, repository publication, and protected-checkout effects independently.

gotchas.summary: A worker can become idle without delivering the final report expected by the controller.
gotchas.countermeasure: Recover the factual report and evidence from the durable transcript instead of inferring completion.

limitations: This procedural guide grants no worker dispatch, file-write, publication, provider, or golden-update authority.
Behavior evidence requires an exact private request and an independently observed fresh-worker run through a trusted host boundary.
